grammar.label: present perfect vs past simple

explanation.en: If you say WHEN, use the past simple. If the time is not finished or not mentioned, use the present perfect.
explanation.uz: Agar QACHON deb aytsangiz — past simple. Vaqt aytilmasa yoki tugamagan bo'lsa — present perfect.

grammar.positive_example: I have seen that film. I saw it last week.
grammar.negative_example: I have seen that film last week.

l1_notes.uz: A1–A2 darajasining ENG qiyin farqi. Qoida oddiy: aniq vaqt bor → past simple.

grammar.label: comparative and superlative adverbs
grammar.form: more quickly, the most carefully; better, worse, faster

explanation.en: Long adverbs take more/most; short ones take -er/-est. 'well' becomes 'better'.

grammar.positive_example: She works more carefully than me.

grammar.label: intensifiers with comparatives
grammar.form: a bit / a little / much / far / a lot + comparative
grammar.meaning: how much bigger the difference is

explanation.en: Use 'much' or 'a lot' for a big difference and 'a bit' for a small one. Never 'very' with a comparative.
explanation.uz: Katta farq uchun 'much' yoki 'a lot'; kichik farq uchun 'a bit'. Qiyosiy daraja bilan 'very' ISHLATILMAYDI.

l1_notes.uz: 'very' faqat oddiy sifat bilan: 'very good', lekin 'much better'.
